> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Extensions Overview

> Optional extensions to the Model Context Protocol

# MCP Extensions

MCP extensions are optional additions to the specification that define capabilities beyond the core protocol. Extensions enable functionality that may be modular (e.g., distinct features like authentication), specialized (e.g., industry-specific logic), or experimental (e.g., features being incubated for potential core inclusion).

Extensions are identified using a unique *extension identifier* with the format: `{vendor-prefix}/{extension-name}`, e.g. `io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials`. Identifiers follow the same rules as [`_meta` keys](/specification/draft/basic/index#meta), with a mandatory prefix. Official extensions use the `io.modelcontextprotocol` vendor prefix.

<Tip>
  If you're building a third-party extension, use a reversed domain name you own as the vendor prefix to avoid collisions (similar to Java package naming). For example, a company owning `example.com` would use `com.example/` as their prefix (e.g., `com.example/my-extension`).
</Tip>

## Official Extension Repositories

Official extensions live inside the [Model Context Protocol GitHub organization](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/) in repositories with the `ext-` prefix.

### MCP Authorization Extensions

<Card title="modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth" icon="github" href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth">
  Extensions for supplementary authorization mechanisms beyond the core
  specification.
</Card>

| Extension | Description |
| - | - |
| [OAuth Client Credentials](/extensions/auth/oauth-client-credentials) | OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow for machine-to-machine authentication. |
| [Enterprise-Managed Authorization](/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization) | Framework for enterprise environments requiring centralized access control. |

### MCP Apps

<Card title="modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps" icon="github" href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps">
  Extensions for interactive UI elements in conversational MCP clients.
</Card>

| Extension | Description |
| - | - |
| [MCP Apps](/extensions/apps/overview) | Allows MCP Servers to display interactive UI elements (charts, forms, video players) inline within conversations |

To get started building MCP Apps, see the [quickstart guide](/extensions/apps/build#getting-started) or read the full [MCP Apps documentation](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/documents/Quickstart.html).

### MCP Tasks

| Extension | Description |
| - | - |
| [MCP Tasks](/extensions/tasks/overview) | Asynchronous task execution for long-running operations, with polling, mid-flight input, and durable handles. |

### Skills over MCP

<Card title="modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills" icon="github" href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills">
  Discover and read Agent Skills from MCP servers.
</Card>

| Extension | Description |
| - | - |
| [Skills over MCP](/extensions/skills/overview) | Discover workflow instructions and read supporting files through MCP resources. |

See the [Skills overview](/extensions/skills/overview) to get started and the
[client matrix](/extensions/client-matrix) for implementation support.

## Experimental Extensions

Experimental extensions provide an incubation pathway for [Working Groups and Interest Groups](/community/working-interest-groups) to prototype ideas and collaborate on extension concepts before formal SEP submission.

Experimental extension repositories live within the MCP GitHub organization with the `experimental-ext-` prefix (e.g., `experimental-ext-interceptors`).

### Ground Rules

* Every experimental extension needs to be associated with a Working Group or Interest Group
* Repositories and published packages need to clearly indicate their experimental status (e.g., in the README and package name)
* [Core Maintainers](/community/contributor-ladder#core-maintainer) retain oversight of experimental extension repositories, including the ability to archive or remove them

### Graduation to Official Status

To promote an experimental extension to official status, it goes through the standard SEP process (Extensions Track). Feel free to reference the experimental repository and any reference implementations you built during incubation to demonstrate the extension's practicality.

## Creating Extensions

The lifecycle for official extensions follows a SEP-based process. For full details, see [SEP-2133: Extensions](/seps/2133-extensions).

1. **Propose**: Create a SEP in the main MCP repository using the [standard SEP guidelines](/community/sep-guidelines) with type **Extensions Track**.
2. **Implement**: Build at least one reference implementation in an official SDK — this is required before the SEP can be reviewed.
3. **Review**: [Core Maintainers](/community/contributor-ladder#core-maintainer) review the SEP and have final authority over inclusion.
4. **Publish**: Once approved, open a PR to add the extension to the extension repository.
5. **Adopt**: After that, other clients, servers, and SDKs can implement the extension too.

### Requirements

* Extension specifications need to use RFC 2119 language (MUST, SHOULD, MAY)
* Extensions must have an associated working group or interest group

### SDK Implementation

SDKs can choose to implement extensions, but it's not required for protocol conformance. SDK maintainers have full autonomy over which extensions they support. Where an SDK does support extensions, SDK documentation should list which extensions are supported.

<Note>
  Extensions are always disabled by default and require explicit opt-in from the developer.
</Note>

### Evolution

Extensions evolve independently of the core protocol. Updates are managed by the extension repository maintainers and don't require core maintainer review.

That said, backwards compatibility matters. When you need to change an extension, prefer using capability flags or versioning within the extension settings object rather than creating a new extension identifier. If a breaking change is unavoidable, use a new identifier (e.g., `io.modelcontextprotocol/my-extension-v2`).

A **breaking change** is any modification that would cause existing implementations to fail or behave incorrectly, including:

* Removing or renaming fields
* Changing field types
* Altering the semantics of existing behavior
* Adding new required fields

## Negotiation

Clients and servers advertise their support for extensions in the `extensions` field within their respective capability declarations.

### Client Capabilities

Clients advertise extension support in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` within each request:

```json theme={null}
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "get_weather",
    "arguments": {
      "location": "New York"
    },
    "_meta": {
      "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
      "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {
        "extensions": {
          "io.modelcontextprotocol/ui": {
            "mimeTypes": ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]
          }
        }
      },
      "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {
        "name": "ExampleClient",
        "version": "1.0.0"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Server Capabilities

Servers advertise extension support in the `server/discover` response:

```json theme={null}
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "resultType": "complete",
    "supportedVersions": ["2026-07-28"],
    "capabilities": {
      "tools": {},
      "extensions": {
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/ui": {}
      }
    },
    "_meta": {
      "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo": {
        "name": "ExampleServer",
        "version": "1.0.0"
      }
    },
    "ttlMs": 3600000,
    "cacheScope": "public"
  }
}
```

Each extension specifies the schema of its settings object; an empty object indicates no settings.

### Graceful Degradation

If one side supports an extension but the other doesn't, the supporting side needs to either fall back to core protocol behavior or reject the request with an appropriate error if the extension is mandatory.

It's a good practice to document expected fallback behavior in your extension. For example, a server offering UI-enhanced tools should still return meaningful text content for clients that don't support the UI extension. On the other hand, a server that requires a specific authentication extension can reject connections from clients that don't support it.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about JetBrains Air and its support for agentic development:

## Overview

JetBrains Air is an "agentic development environment" that lets developers delegate coding tasks to multiple AI agents running concurrently. Out of the box, Air supports Codex, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI, and JetBrains' own Junie.

## AGENTS.md Support

Other agents use AGENTS.md as the primary project instruction file. If your repository contains layered AGENTS.md files, OpenAI Codex uses them to guide task execution.

## Skills Support

Skills are reusable workflows packaged as named units whose main purpose is progressive context disclosure: instead of loading all team guidance into every task, the agent loads the relevant workflow only when it decides to use it.

Shared skills are stored in .agents/skills and are available to all agents in JetBrains Air. Individual agents also have their own skill directories:
- Claude Agent supports agent-specific skills from .claude/skills
- OpenAI Codex supports agent-specific skills from .codex/skills
- Gemini supports agent-specific skills from .gemini/skills
- Junie supports agent-specific skills from .junie/skills

## Plugin Integration

The JetBrains Air in IDEs plugin is compatible with IntelliJ IDEA and other IntelliJ-based IDEs starting from version 2026.2.

# Claude Agent SDK Subagents Guide

## Overview

Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific tasks in isolated context windows. They're useful for:

- **Preserving context** by keeping exploration/implementation separate from main conversation
- **Enforcing constraints** through tool restrictions and permission modes
- **Reusing configurations** across projects with user-level subagents
- **Controlling costs** by routing tasks to faster models like Haiku

## Creating Subagents

### Basic Structure

Subagent files use YAML frontmatter + Markdown system prompt:

```markdown
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for quality and best practices
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
---

You are a code reviewer. When invoked, analyze the code and provide
specific, actionable feedback on quality, security, and best practices.
```

### Key Frontmatter Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier (max 256 chars, no `:` or `-` prefix) |
| `description` | Yes | When Claude should delegate to this subagent |
| `tools` | No | Comma-separated allowed tools; inherits all if omitted |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or full model ID |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan` |
| `memory` | No | `user`, `project`, or `local` for persistent memory |
| `effort` | No | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `maxTurns` | No | Max agentic turns before stopping |
| `isolation` | No | Set to `worktree` for isolated git worktree |
| `skills` | No | Preload skill content into context |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP servers available to this subagent |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) |

## Subagent Scopes

Store subagent files in different locations by priority:

| Location | Scope | Priority |
|----------|-------|----------|
| Managed settings | Organization-wide | 1 (highest) |
| `--agents` CLI flag | Current session | 2 |
| `.claude/agents/` | Current project | 3 |
| `~/.claude/agents/` | All your projects | 4 |
| Plugin `agents/` directory | Where plugin enabled | 5 (lowest) |

## Model Configuration

### Choose a Model

```yaml
---
name: my-agent
model: sonnet  # alias
# OR
model: claude-opus-5-5  # full model ID
# OR
model: inherit  # use main conversation's model
---
```

**Model resolution order:**
1. Per-invocation `model` parameter
2. Subagent definition's `model` field
3. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` environment variable
4. Main conversation's model

### Run All Subagents on One Model

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL": "haiku",
    "CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE": "1"
  }
}
```

## Tool Access Control

### Allowlist Approach
```yaml
---
name: safe-researcher
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
---
```

### Denylist Approach
```yaml
---
name: no-writes
disallowedTools: Write, Edit
---
```

### Restrict Spawned Subagents
```yaml
---
name: coordinator
tools: Agent(worker, researcher), Read, Bash
---
```

Only `worker` and `researcher` subagents can be spawned.

## Permission Modes

```yaml
---
name: my-agent
permissionMode: acceptEdits  # auto-accept edits
---
```

Available modes:
- `default` - Manual mode (prompts for permission)
- `acceptEdits` - Auto-accept file edits in working directory
- `auto` - Auto mode with background classifier
- `dontAsk` - Auto-deny prompts (explicit allows still work)

# Claude Agent SDK Subagents Guide

## Overview

Subagents are specialized AI assistants that handle specific tasks in isolated context windows. They're useful for:

- **Preserving context** by keeping exploration/implementation separate from main conversation
- **Enforcing constraints** through tool restrictions and permission modes
- **Reusing configurations** across projects with user-level subagents
- **Controlling costs** by routing tasks to faster models like Haiku

## Creating Subagents

### Basic Structure

Subagent files use YAML frontmatter + Markdown system prompt:

```markdown
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for quality and best practices
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
---

You are a code reviewer. When invoked, analyze the code and provide
specific, actionable feedback on quality, security, and best practices.
```

### Key Frontmatter Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | Unique identifier (max 256 chars, no `:` or `-` prefix) |
| `description` | Yes | When Claude should delegate to this subagent |
| `tools` | No | Comma-separated allowed tools; inherits all if omitted |
| `model` | No | `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, or full model ID |
| `permissionMode` | No | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan` |
| `memory` | No | `user`, `project`, or `local` for persistent memory |
| `effort` | No | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |
| `maxTurns` | No | Max agentic turns before stopping |
| `isolation` | No | Set to `worktree` for isolated git worktree |
| `skills` | No | Preload skill content into context |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP servers available to this subagent |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) |

## Subagent Scopes

Store subagent files in different locations by priority:

| Location | Scope | Priority |
|----------|-------|----------|
| Managed settings | Organization-wide | 1 (highest) |
| `--agents` CLI flag | Current session | 2 |

# Claude Code Skills Guide

Skills extend Claude's capabilities by bundling instructions, tools, and resources. Here's a comprehensive overview:

## Core Concepts

**What is a skill?** A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter and markdown instructions. When invoked, Claude loads the skill content into context and follows those instructions.

**Key difference from CLAUDE.md:** Skills load on-demand when invoked, while CLAUDE.md is always loaded. This makes skills ideal for large reference material.

## Creating Your First Skill

### Basic Structure
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/my-skill
```

### Minimal SKILL.md
```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: What this skill does
---

Your instructions here...
```

## Where Skills Live

| Location | Path | Available In |
|----------|------|--------------|
| Personal | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | All projects on your machine |
| Project | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | This repo only (commit for team) |
| Enterprise | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in managed settings dir | Organization-wide |
| Nested | `<subdir>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Subdir and below |
| Additional | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` via `--add-dir` | That session only |

## Frontmatter Reference

All fields are optional. Field names use lowercase with hyphens (e.g., `disable-model-invocation`).

### Common Fields

| Field | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `name` | Command name (defaults to directory name) | `name: deploy` → `/deploy` |
| `description` | When Claude should use this skill | `description: Deploy to production` |
| `disable-model-invocation` | Prevent Claude from auto-invoking | `true` for manual-only skills like `/deploy` |
| `user-invocable` | Hide from `/` menu | `false` for background knowledge only |
| `allowed-tools` | Pre-approve tools for this turn | `Bash(git *) Bash(npm *)` |
| `context` | Run in isolated subagent | `context: fork` with optional `agent: Explore` |
| `model` | Override session model | `model: claude-opus-4-1` |
| `effort` | Override effort level | `effort: high` |
| `paths` | Activate only for matching files | `paths: src/**/*.ts,src/**/*.tsx` |
| `shell` | Shell for injected commands | `shell: bash` or `shell: powershell` |
| `argument-hint` | Show in autocomplete | `argument-hint: "[issue-number]"` |
| `arguments` | Named positional arguments | `arguments: [issue, branch]` |

### Advanced Fields

```yaml
background: false              # Wait for forked skill result
hooks: [...]                  # Hooks to register when invoked
metadata: {...}               # Custom YAML for your tooling
```

## Using Skills

### Invoke Manually
```
/my-skill
/my-skill arg1 arg2
```

### Let Claude Invoke Automatically
Write a clear `description` so Claude knows when to use it.

### Stack Multiple Skills
```
/skill1 /skill2 /skill3 argument
```
(Terminal only; up to 6 skills)

## Practical Examples

### Example 1: Git Changes Summary
```yaml
---
name: summarize-changes
description: Summarize uncommitted changes and flag risks
---

## Current changes
!`git diff HEAD`

## Instructions
Summarize in 2-3 bullets, then list any risks (missing error handling, hardcoded values, etc).
```

### Example 2: Deploy Skill (Manual Only)
```yaml
---
name: deploy
description: Deploy to production
disable-model-invocation: true
allowed-tools: Bash(git *) Bash(npm *)
---

Deploy $ARGUMENTS to production:

1. Run test suite
2. Build application
3. Push to deployment target
4. Verify deployment
```

### Example 3: Research with Forked Agent
```yaml
---
name: research
description: Deep research on a topic
context: fork
agent: Explore
---

Research $ARGUMENTS:

1. Find relevant files using Glob/Grep
2. Read and analyze code
3. Summarize findings with file references
```

## Dynamic Context Injection

Use `` !`command` `` to run shell commands before Claude sees the skill:

```yaml
---
name: pr-review
description: Review pull request
---

## PR Diff
!`gh pr diff`

## PR Comments
!`gh pr view --comments`

## Your Task
Review this PR...
```

### Multi-line Commands
````markdown
```!
node --version
git status --short
```
````

## Argument Handling

### Using Arguments
```yaml
---
name: fix-issue
description: Fix a GitHub issue
arguments: [issue_number]
---

Fix issue $issue_number following our standards.
```

### Invocation
- `/fix-issue 123` → `$issue_number` becomes `123`
- `$ARGUMENTS` → all args as one string
- `$0`, `$1`, etc. → positional access
- `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` → skill directory path
- `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` → project root

## Controlling Invocation

| Setting | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| `disable-model-invocation: true` | Claude can't auto-invoke; only `/name` works |
| `user-invocable: false` | Hide from `/` menu; Claude-only |
| Default (both omitted) | Both you and Claude can invoke |

## Skill Lifecycle

- **Rendered once** when invoked
- **Stays in context** across turns
- **Costs tokens** every turn it remains
- **Auto-compaction** keeps recently-used skills after context fills up
- **`allowed-tools` grants** clear after your next message

## Supporting Files

Keep `SKILL.md` concise (~500 lines max). Add supporting files:

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md
├── reference.md
├── examples.md
└── scripts/helper.sh
```

Reference in SKILL.md:
```markdown
For API details: [reference.md](reference.md)
For examples: [examples.md](examples.md)
```

## Managing Skills

### Remove a Skill
- **Personal/Project**: Delete the directory
- **Enterprise**: Admin removes from managed settings
- **Plugin**: Disable/uninstall the plugin
- **Synced from claude.ai**: Turn off in account settings

### Hide Without Deleting
Set in `skillOverrides` in `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "skillOverrides": {
    "legacy-context": "name-only",
    "deploy": "off"
  }
}
```

States: `"on"` (default), `"name-only"`, `"user-invocable-only"`, `"off"`

### Disable All Skills
Add to permission deny rules:
```
Skill
```

## Bundled Skills

Claude Code includes built-in skills: `/doctor`, `/code-review`, `/debug`, `/verify`, `/run`, etc.

To disable: Set `disableBundledSkills: true` in settings.

## Advanced: Forked Skills

Use `context: fork` to run in an isolated subagent:

```yaml
---
name: complex-task
context: fork
agent: Explore           # Optional: Explore, Plan, general-purpose
background: false       # Wait for result (default: true)
---

Task instructions here...
```

The subagent:
- Doesn't see your conversation history
- Has isolated context (small for Explore/Plan agents)
- Returns results when complete
- Runs in background by default

## Skill Evaluation

Use the [skill-creator plugin](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/plugins/skill-creator) to:
- Create baseline test cases
- Run evals with/without the skill
- Measure token cost vs. improvement
- A/B test skill versions
- Grade outputs against assertions

Install:
```
/plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official
```

## Best Practices

✅ **Do:**
- Write clear descriptions so Claude knows when to use it
- Keep SKILL.md focused; move large references to supporting files
- Use `disable-model-invocation: true` for side-effect commands
- Test with `skill-creator` for iteration
- Commit project skills to version control

❌ **Don't:**
- Make SKILL.md > 500 lines
- Forget that skill content stays in context (costs tokens)
- Use injected commands (`!`) in synced claude.ai skills
- Put secrets in skill content

## Synced Skills from claude.ai

If you use Cowork, cloud sessions, or sign in via claude.ai account:
- Skills sync to `~/.claude/skills/synced/`
- Full name: `/anthropic-skills:skill-name`
- Short name available if no local skill conflicts
- Never edit synced skills locally (updates are overwritten)

To manage: Enable/disable in claude.ai settings.

Z2 "Agent Plugins excludes hooks, commands, agents, marketplaces, permissions, trust": spec lists commands, hooks, agents, rules, LSP as out-of-v1 component types; AAIF blog lists distribution (registries, marketplaces), runtime (permissions, sandbox, UI), trust, client-specific.   "version": "3.0.3",
  "description": "Shipping plugin ...",

  "repository": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
  "keywords": ["shipping"],
  "extensions": { "dev.orindx.wisp": { "consumes": [], "produces": ["changeset@2","release-artifact@2"], "agents": ["./agents/changeset-analyzer.md"] } }
}
```

No third-party marketplace mechanism is documented. A search snippet says "marketplace defined by marketplace.json with relative paths, GitHub repos" [S, unconfirmed on a Google page]. 3. Z2 "Agent Plugins 1.0.0 ... Working draft": spec says Status: Published.

8. Z2 "Agent Plugins excludes hooks, commands, agents, marketplaces, permissions, trust": spec lists commands, hooks, agents, rules, LSP as out-of-v1 component types; AAIF blog lists distribution (registries, marketplaces), runtime (permissions, sandbox, UI), trust, client-specific. ## 4. Minimal convergence manifest
Root `plugins/<id>/plugin.json` (valid under Agent Plugins 1.0.0, AGY, Cursor-AgentPlugins; Claude ignores unknown keys):
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "courier",
  "version": "3.0.3",
  "description": "Shipping plugin ...",
  "author": { "name": "Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)", "email": "gabe@techworx.dev" },
  "license": "MIT",
  "repository": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
  "keywords": ["shipping"],
  "extensions": { "dev.orindx.wisp": { "consumes": [], "produces": ["changeset@2","release-artifact@2"], "agents": ["./agents/changeset-analyzer.md"] } }
}
```
- Drop top-level id/skills/agents/consumes/produces (move to `extensions.<reverse-domain>`; our tooling reads from there).
- Claude: add `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (can be a copy minus `$schema`, or the same file via generator) so version/description/author register; optional since Claude auto-discovers skills/ and agents/.
- AGY: same root plugin.json works; agents/ files need AGY frontmatter (model inherit/flash/pro, tools) to take effect, via generated overlay or by relying on defaults (AGY agents with unknown fields: undocumented).
- Replace the `shared` symlink with a generated in-root copy at build time (or hoist references into each plugin).
- Move SKILL.md `version` under `metadata:`; run `skills-ref validate`.
- Marketplace: keep .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (Claude, valid). Delete or relabel root marketplace.json: it is not an AGY artifact; remove the 404 `$schema`.

## 5. PLAN IMPACT vs ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md
- Row 12 "AGY's plugin format is similar to Claude's": TRUE for components (plugin.json at root of a dir with skills/, agents/, mcp, hooks, rules); DIFFERENT in: manifest location (root vs .claude-plugin/), manifest fields (AGY documents 3), mcp file (mcp_config.json vs .mcp.json), hooks (hooks.json at root vs hooks/hooks.json), agent frontmatter (flash/pro vs haiku/sonnet/opus), marketplace (official-only vs user marketplaces), install unit (single-plugin repo URL or local dir vs marketplace add). Claude and AGY are not "two trees" today: the repo already ships ONE authored tree that AGY can install per plugin via local path; the real trees are authored, generated Codex (dist/codex, harnesses/codex), and per-harness overlays. Reframe as "one authored tree + generated overlays: Claude manifest, AGY agent/hooks, Codex".
- WP-610 corrections: (a) the portable core is a manifest everyone can read, not a Claude/AGY convergence: Agent Plugins does not name either; AGY follows its own near-superset; (b) required work item: add `$schema` + move custom keys under `extensions` (otherwise AP clients REJECT the plugin, i.e. Cursor/Copilot/Kiro/VS Code/Codex portable installs fail); (c) fix symlink; (d) fix SKILL.md `version`; (e) "re-verify AGY marketplace schema" result: it does not exist publicly; remove it and the 404 `$schema`, and say AGY distribution = `agy plugin install <github-url|local path>` (one repo or subpath per plugin) or the Google-curated official marketplace via the interest form.
- AGY install of the monorepo by GitHub URL cannot work as-is (no plugin.json at repo root); document `agy plugin install plugins/<id>` locally or publish per-plugin repos [I: GitHub-subdir install is not documented].
- WP-616: AGY workflow date confirmed [P] 2026-10-19; this repo ships no workflows, so no action. Claude has its own `workflows` plugin component (JS) unrelated to AGY workflows: do not conflate.
- WP-607 evidence: AGY browser subagent saves screenshots and videos as artifacts [P, thin page]; Gemini model names in Z2 are stale.
- MCP (WP-614): spec is 2026-07-28; Tasks and MCP Apps are Extensions (opt-in, negotiated); Skills over MCP extension exists and could ship skills with a server; the Agent Plugins mcp.json uses its own closed schema (`type` required, `mcpServers`, `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`) distinct from Claude `.mcp.json` and AGY `mcp_config.json`: three MCP config file names.
- Skill portability: AGY, Copilot, Kiro, Air, Cursor, Codex all load Agent Skills folders; paths differ (.agents/skills is the common one: AGY, Copilot, Air). Authoring skills into `.agents/skills`-compatible form is the widest reach. Rules/hooks/agents remain per-harness.
- Unverified: whether Claude, AGY actually reject/warn on `role`, `version`; install behavior of dangling symlink; skills-ref strictness; Cursor/Copilot/Kiro install of our layout (Cursor and AP clients would reject for missing `$schema`; Copilot/Kiro plugin load unverified).

Full report: /Users/gabe/.claude/jobs/2d213021/tmp/Y4-agy-standards.md. It has the fact table with quotes, CORRECTIONS vs Z2, the conformance table, a minimal convergence manifest, and PLAN IMPACT.

**Conformance defects (highest severity first)**
1. Root `marketplace.json` has `$schema` https://antigravity.google/schemas/marketplace.json, which returns 404. The documented AGY plugin schema (/schemas/v1/plugin.json) also returns 404. AGY docs say "<marketplace-name> only supports the official marketplace, antigravity-plugins-official". No third-party marketplace.json is documented, so that file is a repo-private manifest, not an AGY artifact. Its `id`, `path` and `supersedes` fields are ours alone.
2. Every `plugins/*/plugin.json` lacks `$schema`. In Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (Status: Published), `$schema` and `name` are required. A missing `$schema` is a fatal schema violation, and the client rejects the plugin. Unknown top-level keys (`id`, `skills`, `agents`, `consumes`, `produces`) are report-and-ignore. Claude strips them with a warning, and AGY documents only name, description and $schema.
3. Claude Code reads only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Our manifests sit at the plugin root, so Claude never sees them. Skills and agents still load through default discovery, but the name comes from the marketplace entry and the version, description and author are lost.
4. Each plugin has a `shared -> ../../shared` symlink that leaves the plugin root. Agent Plugins §4.1 requires clients to reject such paths. I did not test install behavior, but a subdir copy likely leaves it dangling [inference].
5. Agent frontmatter uses `model: haiku/sonnet/opus`, `effort` and `role`. Claude accepts `model` and `effort` and ignores `role`. AGY subagents accept `model: inherit/flash/pro` and use AGY tool names, so our tier mapping would not apply there. Agent Plugins excludes agents entirely.
6. All 30 SKILL.md files have a top-level `version`. The Agent Skills spec has no such field (it belongs under `metadata`). `skills-ref` may flag it; I did not run it. Names equal directory names and all descriptions are under 1024 characters.

**Contradictions with Z2**
- Only `name` is required by AGY; `$schema` is optional.
- Agent Plugins is "Published", not a working draft.
- The AGY workflow shutdown on 2026-10-19 is confirmed on the primary migration page. A search snippet saying Nov 1 is wrong.
- AGY's model list is Gemini 4 Argon / 3.8 Flash plus Claude 5.5, not "3.5 Flash".
- Agent Plugins' named clients are Kiro, Cursor, Grok Bot, VS Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, NanoClaw, ChatGPT & Codex, GitHub Copilot and OpenHands. Neither Claude Code nor AGY is named.
- `when_to_use` is not in the Skills spec.
- The AGY "marketplace gap" is bigger than Z2 said: third-party marketplaces are not documented at all.

**Plan impact**
- The "AGY is similar to Claude" framing holds for components (`skills/`, `agents/`, hooks, MCP, `rules/`). It differs in manifest location, MCP and hooks filenames, agent frontmatter, and distribution.
- "Two trees" is the wrong frame. The repo already has one authored tree. AGY can install a plugin from a local path, but a GitHub URL install needs a plugin at the repo root, which the monorepo lacks [documented install forms only; subdir install is inference]. The real divergences are the Codex generated tree and per-harness overlays.
- WP-610 should:
  - add `$schema` and move custom keys under `extensions."<reverse-domain>"`;
  - add `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`;
  - replace the `shared` symlink with a build-time copy;
  - move SKILL.md `version` under `metadata`;
  - generate AGY agent frontmatter;
  - drop the AGY marketplace schema and its 404 `$schema`.
- The MCP 2026-07-28 changes are confirmed from the changelog. Tasks and MCP Apps are opt-in Extensions. Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated, with a 12-month floor.
- Unverified: actual install behavior in each harness, Copilot and Kiro plugin loading of our layout, and whether `skills-ref` rejects `version`.
